policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere לעזור and ketiv לעזיר are spellings of the same infinitive 'to help'; ASV 'to succor us' renders either. The versional note on this verse concerns 'thou art worth ten thousand of us', not this unit.
Qere נפצת and ketiv נפצית are orthographic variants of the same feminine participle 'spread'; ASV 'was there spread over' renders either. No note.

ASV 'Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver ... yet would I not' renders the concessive/conditional particle לוא of the qere; the ketiv ולא 'and not' would give a plain negation with no 'though'. The hebrew_gloss note concerns 'Beware that none touch', not this unit.
ASV text 'against his life' renders the ketiv בנפשו (3ms suffix); the textual_variant note 'Another reading is, my' names the qere בנפשי as the alternative the ASV did not follow.
ASV 'every one to his tent' is singular, matching the ketiv לאהלו 'his tent'; the qere לאהליו is plural 'his tents', which the ASV wording does not reflect.
Qere בחייו and ketiv בחיו are plene/defective spellings of the same word 'in his life'; ASV 'in his lifetime' renders either. No note.

ASV 'because the king's son is dead' renders the following כי; the qere על־כן 'therefore' adds a connective the ASV does not print, but English translators routinely drop a redundant 'therefore' before 'because', so the absence does not exclude the qere. No note.
